chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: A deterministic process in which an argument causes conviction can still be rational, so involuntary causal belief formation does not by itself discredit reasoning.

orphanFallback.rationale: The same proposition constructively establishes that causal determination and rational responsiveness are compatible, using argument-induced conviction as its source-grounded example.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Experience and selection can support abstraction and memory, while human difficulty with quantum and cosmic scales is expected because those capacities did not evolve specifically for advanced science.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive account, the proposition links abstraction and memory to experience and adaptive value while treating difficulty outside ancestral scales as an expected evolutionary limitation.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Deductive conclusions preserve the semantic content of their premises through tautological transformation, and their validity rests on necessary logical relations available under naturalism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently grounds deductive trust in content preservation and necessary logical relations, providing a positive naturalistic account without needing a preceding objection.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: A physically constituted whole can represent something even though its atomic constituents do not, as illustrated by a book that is about a subject despite being made of non-intentional atoms.

orphanFallback.rationale: The book analogy positively supports the source-grounded part-to-whole possibility that physical constitution does not prevent a system from possessing representational aboutness.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Natural selection can favor investigative and classificatory capacities that track real environmental dangers and benefits reliably enough to support rational inference.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition supplies a freestanding evolutionary mechanism: organisms that investigate and accurately classify consequential features of their environment predictably gain a survival advantage.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: An incomplete naturalistic explanation of consciousness does not itself warrant supernatural agency, especially when broader neuroscientific success counsels against a hasty gap inference.

orphanFallback.rationale: Constructively stated, the proposition sets an evidential standard under which present explanatory incompleteness is insufficient positive support for a supernatural cause.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Awareness can develop gradually as increasingly complex organisms progress from simple environmental responsiveness through pleasure, pain, desire, and eventually abstract thought.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition itself provides a positive, source-grounded naturalistic pathway from elementary responsiveness to affective awareness and higher cognition.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Conscious awareness may confer an evolutionary advantage or arise as a harmless byproduct, and either evolutionary origin remains compatible with the accuracy of resulting reasoning.

orphanFallback.rationale: As an independent constructive distinction, the proposition separates consciousness's adaptive origin from the accuracy of cognition and identifies two naturalistically compatible origins.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: The long, gradual, trial-and-error development of conscious rational creatures with intermediate capacities is more expected under natural evolution than under divine or supernatural agency.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently makes a comparative likelihood case from the observed gradual, complex, and trial-dependent mechanism of cognitive development to naturalistic expectation.
